questions.question: The perimeter of a triangle with sides of integer values is equal to 13. How many such triangles are possible?
questions.questionHtml: The perimeter of a triangle with sides of integer values is equal to 13. How many such triangles are possible?
questions.solution:
If p = odd, then t = (p + 3)2/48   [ where p is perimeter and t is total possible triangles ]

Total possible triangles = (13 + 3)2/48 ⇒ 5.33 ≈ 5

questions.question: The ratio of number of sides of two regular polygons is 4 : 5 and the ratio of their internal angles are 15 : 16. The number of sides of the polygons is:
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of number of sides of two regular polygons is 4 : 5 and the ratio of their internal angles are 15 : 16. The number of sides of the polygons is:
questions.solution:
Let the sides be 4x and 5x.

Internal angle of a n-sided polygon = (n - 2)/n × 180° 

⇒ {(4x - 2)/4x × 180°}/{(5x - 2)/5x × 180°} = 15/16

⇒ (4x - 2)/(5x - 2) × 5/4 = 15/16

⇒ (4x - 2)/(5x - 2) = 3/4

⇒ 16x - 8 = 15x - 6 ⇒ x = 8 - 6 = 2

So, the number of sides of the two polygons is 8 and 10.

questions.question: In ΔABC, the length of BC is less than twice the length of AB by 2 cm. The length of AC exceeds the length of AB by 6 cm. The perimeter is 60 cm. The length (in cm) of the largest side of the triangle ABC is:
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, the length of BC is less than twice the length of AB by 2 cm. The length of AC exceeds the length of AB by 6 cm. The perimeter is 60 cm. The length (in cm) of the largest side of the triangle ABC is:
questions.solution:
Given:

The perimeter of Δ ABC = 60 cm.

Calculation:

Let the length of AB be x cm

So, the length of BC = (2x - 2) cm and the length of AC = (x + 6) cm

The perimeter of Δ ABC = 60 cm.

⇒ x + 2x - 2 + x + 6 = 60

⇒ 4x + 4 = 60

⇒ 4x = 56

⇒ x = 14

The lengths of the sides of the triangle are:

AB = 14 cm

BC = (2x - 2) cm = 26 cm

AC = (x + 6) = 20 cm

∴ The length of the largest side of the triangle is 26 cm.

questions.question: If a, b and c are the sides of a right-angled triangle, where a > b > c, then what is the value of the expression (a + b + c) (a + b - c) (a - b + c) (a - b - c)?
questions.questionHtml:
If a, b and c are the sides of a right-angled triangle, where a > b > c, then what is the value of the expression

(a + b + c) (a + b - c) (a - b + c) (a - b - c)?

options.html: 4b2c2
-4b2c2
-2a2b2
-4a2b2

questions.solution:
Given:

If a, b, c are sides of a right angle triangle, where a> b> c

Calculation:

Let's assume the sides of right angles triangle be 3, 4, and 5

Therefore,

⇒ (a + b + c) (a + b - c) ( a - b + c) (a - b - c)

⇒ (5 + 4 + 3) (5 + 4 - 3) (5 - 4 + 3) (5 - 4 - 3)

⇒ (12) (6) (4) (-2) = - 576

From the options,

Option1 → 4b2c2 = 4(42)(32) = 576

Option2 → -4b2c2 = -4(42)(32) = - 576

Option3 → -2a2b2 = -2(52)(42) = - 800

Option4 → -4a2b2  = -4(52)(42) = - 1600    

∴ (a + b + c) (a + b - c) (a - b + c) ( a - b - c) = -4b2c2

questions.question: In an isosceles triangle, if the unequal angle is 4 times the sum of the equal angles, then each equal angle is:
questions.questionHtml: In an isosceles triangle, if the unequal angle is 4 times the sum of the equal angles, then each equal angle is:
questions.solution:
Concept used:

In a Δ ABC, A + B + C = 180° 

Calculation:

Let ΔABC be an isosceles triangle, where side AB = AC

So, ∠B = ∠C

Let ∠B = ∠C = x

According to the given data,

∠A = 4 (x + x) = 4 × 2x = 8x

according to the concept,

⇒ 8x + x + x = 180∘

⇒ 10x = 180∘

⇒ x = 18∘

∴ The value of each equal angle is 18°

questions.question: What is the area (in unit squares) of the triangle enclosed by the graphs of 2x + 5y = 12, x + y = 3 and the x-axis?
questions.questionHtml: What is the area (in unit squares) of the triangle enclosed by the graphs of 2x + 5y = 12, x + y = 3 and the x-axis?
questions.solution:
Point of intersection of equation-  (2x + 5y) - (2x + 2y) = 12 - 2 × 3 ⇒ 3y = 6 ⇒ y = 2 

⇒ x = 1

Base (AB) = 6 - 3 = 3 unit, Height (CM) = Y-coordinate = 2 unit.

questions.question: The minimuim number of acute angle in a triangle is ________
questions.questionHtml: The minimuim number of acute angle in a triangle is ________
questions.solution:
Concept

The least number of acute angles that a triangle can have is 2.

Solution

Because if a triangle has more than one obtuse angle or right angle the sum of all angles will be greater than 180° , which is not possible in a triangle.

Hence, the least number of acute angles that a triangle can have is 2.

questions.question: In a ΔABC, AB = 6 cm, BC = 11 cm, how many integral value of AC can be possible to draw a ΔABC ?
questions.questionHtml: In a ΔABC, AB = 6 cm, BC = 11 cm, how many integral value of AC can be possible to draw a ΔABC?
questions.solution:
Given:

In a ΔABC,

AB = 6 cm and BC = 11 cm

Formula used:

In ΔABC,

Conditions for drawing a triangle:

The sum of two sides is more than the length of the third side.

(1.1) a + b > c

(1.2) a + c > b

(1.3) c + b > a

The difference of the two sides is less than the length of the third side.

(2.1) |b - c| < a

(2.2) |a - c| < b

(2.3) |a - b| < c

Calculation:

According to the question,

Let,

AB = c = 6 cm

BC = a = 11 cm

AC = b

Since the sum of two sides is more than the length of the third side,

Therefore, 

⇒ b < 11 + 6

⇒ b < 17          ----(1)

Since the difference of the two sides is less than the length of the third side,

Therefore, 

⇒ b > 11 - 6

⇒ b > 5          ----(2)

On combining the equation (1) and (2), we get,

⇒ 5 < b < 17

The possible length of AC can be 6 cm, 7 cm, 8 cm, 9 cm, 10 cm, 11 cm, 12 cm,  13 cm,  14 cm, 15 cm and 16 cm.

The possible length of AC is 11.

Therefore, '11' is the required answer.

Shortcut Trick 

In ΔABC,

AB = c = 6 cm, BC = a = 11 cm,

The number of the integral value of AC can be possible to draw a ΔABC = 2n - 1

Where n is the minimum value between a and c.

According to the question,

⇒ n = c = 6

Now,

The number of the integral values of AC can be possible to draw a ΔABC = 2n - 1

⇒ 2 × 6 -1 = 12 -1 = 11

Therefore, '11' is the required answer.

questions.question: In triangle PQR , if ∠P - ∠Q = 14° and ∠Q - ∠R = 29 ° , then ∠Q =
questions.questionHtml: In triangle PQR, if ∠P - ∠Q = 14° and ∠Q - ∠R = 29°, then ∠Q =
questions.solution:
Given:

∠P - ∠Q = 14°

∠Q - ∠R = 29°

Concept used: 

Sum of interior angles of a triangle = 180° 

Calculation:

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q + ∠R = 180° → (1)

⇒ ∠P - ∠Q = 14°

⇒ ∠P = 14° + ∠Q  → (2)

⇒ ∠Q - ∠R = 29°

⇒ ∠R = ∠Q - 29° → (3)

⇒ 14° + ∠Q + ∠Q + ∠Q - 29° = 180° 

⇒ 3∠Q = 180° + 15° 

⇒ 3∠ Q = 195° 

∴  ∠ Q = 65°

questions.question: In the figure given above, ABC is an equilateral triangle of side length 30 cm. XY is parallel to BC, XP is parallel to AC and YQ is parallel to AB. If (XY + XP + YQ) is 40 cm, then what is PQ equal to?
questions.questionHtml: In the figure given above, ABC is an equilateral triangle of side length 30 cm. XY is parallel to BC, XP is parallel to AC and YQ is parallel to AB. If (XY + XP + YQ) is 40 cm, then what is PQ equal to?
questions.solution:
Concept used:

Corresponding angles: If two lines are parallel then the pair of corresponding angles are equal.

       

In the above figure, if AB ∥ CD then,

  • ∠1 = ∠5
  • ∠2 = ∠6
  • ∠4 = ∠8
  • ∠3 = ∠7

Calculation:

It is given that, XP ∥ AC

So, ∠XPB = ∠C = 60° {corresponding angles} 

In ΔXPB,

⇒ ∠B + ∠XPB + ∠BXP = 180° 

⇒ 60° + 60° + ∠BXP = 180° 

⇒ ∠BXP = 60° 

Hence, ΔBXP is an equilateral triangle.

Similarly, ΔCYQ is also an equilateral triangle.

In □XYCP

⇒ XP ∥ YC & XY ∥ PC

Hence, □XYCP is a parallelogram.

Similarly, □XYQB is also a parallelogram.

⇒ XY + XP + YQ = 40

Since, XY = PC & XP = BP

⇒ (PC + BP) + YQ = 40 

⇒ 30 + YQ = 40

⇒ YQ = 10 cm = QC

Similarly, XP = BP = 10 cm

⇒ BP + PQ + QC = 30

⇒ 10 + PQ + 10 = 30

⇒ PQ = 10 cm

∴ The value of PQ is 10 cm.
